outages.cause: Rolling and emergency blackouts after Russian attacks on energy infrastructure
outages.affected: Ukrenergo said that on Monday, Nov 16, hourly rolling blackouts of 1 to 3 queues, plus industrial capacity limits, are in effect through the end of the day in parts of Ukraine. UNN, citing Ukrenergo, said one queue is four hours, so Monday's outages may last from 4 to 12 hours. Ukraine's Energy Ministry said that after Russian attacks overnight and Monday morning, some consumers were without power as of Monday morning in the Vinnytsia, Dnipropetrovsk, Kirovohrad, Odesa, Ternopil, and Cherkasy regions; it did not give customer counts for those regions. Interfax-Ukraine, citing Ukrenergo, said emergency outage schedules were applied in the morning in the Kharkiv and Poltava regions. DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi said a Russian attack on the morning of Nov 16 on its facilities in the north of Odesa region left 52,200 households without power (see the separate Northern Odesa region row). No later official Ukrenergo Monday schedule change was found. On the Nov 15 Zaporizhzhia attack, Zaporizhzhiaoblenergo, as reported by Interfax-Ukraine, said electricity supply to 359,000 consumers in Zaporizhzhia and the region was disrupted and that after critical infrastructure was restored in 4.5 hours, power was returned to 359,000 households and legal entities a few hours later; Mykhailo Semikin, acting head of the Zaporizhzhia Regional Military Administration, had said Sunday evening that power supply had been restored in the Zaporizhzhia region, according to Ukrinform at 9:00 p.m. EET. For Dnipropetrovsk, the Energy Ministry said some consumers remained without power Monday morning after the attacks; no official customer count or later restoration notice was found. Overnight Nov 15 outages: DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi said in a Nov 15 statement that a Russian attack overnight on one of its energy facilities left 41,000 customers without power (no later official restoration figure found; see the separate Odesa region, including Chornomorsk, row). Sumyoblenergo, in a Nov 16 update reported by SUMYTODAY, said part of Sumy region was still without a stable electricity supply for a second day after an accident at a high-voltage facility (no customer count). On Friday, Nov 13, Chernihivoblenergo said an attack left about 150,000 customers without power in the Nizhyn and Pryluky districts; no later Chernihiv customer figure or confirmed restoration was found.

outages.cause: Russian attack on DTEK energy facilities
outages.affected: 52,200 households without power, according to a Nov 16 statement by DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi. DTEK said a Russian attack on the morning of Nov 16 hit its energy facilities in the north of Odesa region, that 52,200 households were temporarily left without electricity, that specialists were inspecting surviving equipment in order to begin repairs as soon as possible, and that all work is being carried out under safety rules, including during air-raid alerts. DTEK also said the company's production site was damaged in the attack (windows blown out and ceilings and doors damaged) and that employees were not injured. No restoration time was given. This is a separate, later attack in the north of the region from DTEK's Nov 14 statement that a morning attack on one of its facilities there left almost 50,000 customers without power, and from the overnight Nov 15 DTEK attack that left 41,000 households without power in the Odesa region. No later official customer count or restoration notice was found after the morning Nov 16 statement.
outages.updated: Nov 16, 2026 (DTEK OEM statement, dated Nov 16); Ukrinform 11:42 a.m. EET Monday (= 3:42 a.m. CT), citing DTEK; rechecked 5:55 AM CT Monday, no later official restoration figure found

outages.cause: Russian attack on a DTEK energy facility
outages.affected: 41,000 customers without power, according to a Nov 15 statement by DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi. DTEK said a Russian attack overnight on Nov 15 hit one of its energy facilities, that 41,000 customers were left without electricity, that crews began work once it was safe, that specialists were inspecting surviving equipment, clearing rubble, and making repairs, that restoration will take a long time, and that air-raid alerts were significantly complicating the work. No restoration time was given. Oleh Kiper, head of the Odesa Regional Military Administration, said around 41,000 customers were temporarily left without electricity after a strike on a DTEK Odesa Electricity Networks facility. Ukraine's State Emergency Service said Russia attacked Chornomorsk; reporting on the same overnight attack said the city was left without power and that six people were injured. This is a separate outage from the morning Nov 16 DTEK attack in the north of Odesa region that left 52,200 households without power. No later official customer count or restoration notice was found.
outages.updated: Nov 15, 2026, DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi official statement (dated Nov 15); LB.ua 10:11 a.m. EET (= 2:11 a.m. CT), citing Oleh Kiper and the State Emergency Service; rechecked 5:55 AM CT Monday, no later official restoration figure found

outages.place: Mariupol, Donetsk, Volnovakha, Novoazovsk, and nearby cities
outages.cause: Occupation authorities said energy infrastructure was attacked on the nights of Nov 15 and Nov 16, causing an emergency in the regional power system. On Nov 15, the Russia-appointed head of the Donetsk occupation government, Andrey Chertkov, said the grid was damaged by a "powerful enemy attack," while some Russian media called it an accident. Vedomosti reported that Ukrainian forces struck energy infrastructure in the region overnight Nov 15
outages.affected: Occupation authorities issued new figures on the morning of Nov 16 and did not give a single official total for the whole region. The occupation-appointed mayor of Donetsk, Alexey Kulemzin, citing Donetskenergo (a branch of JSC Yugo-Zapadnaya ESK), said 1,493 transformer substations remained partially de-energized in all districts of Donetsk and that 201,220 subscribers remained without electricity, with restoration work continuing, according to a Nov 16, 10:55 a.m. local report on news-donetsk.ru. The occupation administration of the Mariupol urban district, as reported by MRPL.NEWS at 9:41 a.m. local Nov 16, said that as of the morning of Nov 16 more than 133,500 subscribers in Mariupol remained without electricity and that 941 transformer substations in the urban district remained de-energized; it said emergency restoration work was continuing and that customers were being reconnected in stages as technical conditions allowed, and it gave no time for full restoration. A Nov 16 morning statement from the occupation Ministry of Coal and Energy, as carried by newsmariupol.ru at 9:37 a.m. local, said energy infrastructure in the occupied Donetsk region and neighboring occupied Luhansk region had been attacked on the nights of Nov 15 and Nov 16, that outages the previous day had affected practically the entire territory of the occupied Donetsk region, that crews had restored power to some consumers overnight but that large-scale outages remained, and that it was not possible to give an exact time for full restoration. These figures come from occupation authorities and were not independently confirmed in the sources reviewed. No later official restoration notice was found.
outages.updated: Nov 16, 2026, Mariupol occupation administration via MRPL.NEWS 9:41 a.m. local Monday (= 12:41 a.m. CT); Kulemzin / Donetskenergo via news-donetsk.ru 10:55 a.m. local Monday (= 1:55 a.m. CT); occupation Ministry of Coal and Energy via newsmariupol.ru 9:37 a.m. local Monday (= 12:37 a.m. CT); Nov 15 ministry and Chertkov statements via dnrnews.ru, Vedomosti, and RFE/RL; rechecked 5:55 AM CT Monday, no later official restoration notice found

outages.cause: Generation capacity deficit, with several thermoelectric units offline due to breakdowns (Santa Cruz unit 1, Antonio Guiteras, Felton unit 2, and Renté unit 3) and maintenance (Santa Cruz unit 3, Nuevitas unit 5, Felton unit 1, and Renté unit 5); thermal generation is also limited by 251 MW
outages.affected: UNE's Sunday bulletin, published by Cubadebate and attributed to UNE-MINEM, remained the latest official national forecast found: 1,860 MW affected at the evening peak, 970 MW available versus 2,800 MW demand (1,830 MW deficit), if the forecast conditions hold. At 6:00 a.m. Sunday, the grid had 925 MW available versus 2,265 MW of demand, leaving 1,340 MW unserved, and UNE estimated 1,500 MW affected at midday. UNE said Renté unit 3 was expected to add 45 MW at the Sunday evening peak. On Saturday, service was affected by a generation-capacity deficit for all 24 hours and remained affected through the early morning; the maximum Saturday affectation was 1,878 MW at 7:00 p.m. Saturday solar photovoltaic output was 3,116 MWh, with a maximum of 485 MW at midday. No official Sunday midday or evening-peak actual was found, and no official Monday UNE national bulletin had been published as of this recheck. CiberCuba, in a Nov 16 compilation updated at 6:15 a.m. Cuba time Monday, said it was still showing Sunday's figures because Monday's bulletin did not yet contain sufficient numbers, and that the national grid was not recorded as in a total collapse. On Monday morning, Empresa Eléctrica de La Habana reported generation-deficit interruptions, including from 4:39 a.m. Cuba time on circuits MB950 (Ampliación de Marbella, Guanabo, Bello Monte, and Villa del Mar) and MB910/D1055 (Justi, Agromar, Bajurayabo, Campo Florido, La Coca, and the Las Minas, Gallega, and Arango neighborhoods), from 4:08 a.m. on circuit R464 (Reparto Modelo, Alturas de Vía Blanca, Habana Nueva, La Cotorra, and Villa1), and from 4:03 a.m. on circuit P317 (25 y K); it also reported restorations on circuit A1430 (Soterrado Cujae, Toledo) at 4:52 a.m. and circuit S516 at 4:06 a.m., according to the same CiberCuba compilation. A possible Monday startup of the Antonio Guiteras plant had been described as a forecast, not a confirmed return to service.
outages.updated: Nov 15, 2026, UNE Sunday bulletin via Cubadebate (attributed to UNE-MINEM); Empresa Eléctrica de La Habana Monday morning circuit reports via CiberCuba compilation updated 6:15 a.m. Cuba time Monday, Nov 16 (= 5:15 a.m. CT), including 4:03–4:52 a.m. Cuba time Monday reports (= 3:03–3:52 a.m. CT); rechecked 5:55 AM CT Monday, no official Sunday midday or evening-peak actual and no Monday UNE national bulletin found

outages.place: Mayfair West, Amalgam, Vrededorp, Pageview, and nearby Johannesburg suburbs
outages.cause: Fire and a later explosion at the Mayfair substation; after a Thursday-night restoration, the Hursthill substation tripped early Friday because of a network overload. City Power later said the first explosion was caused by cable theft. A separate Crown Substation fault and a Florida Glen cable theft also interrupted supply. On Sunday, City Power said a 16-hour emergency shutdown was needed to complete critical Mayfair Substation repairs
outages.affected: No official customer count. SABC News, in a 10:01 a.m. SAST Monday, Nov 16 report, quoted City Power spokesperson Isaac Mangena saying that restoration shortly after midnight had brought several critical customers and sections of the network back online, including the SABC and Netcare Garden City Hospital, and that restoration work was continuing. He said parts of Crown remained outstanding and were scheduled to receive attention on Monday, and that technicians were also attending to further cable faults affecting customers in Mayfair West, Amalgam, Vrededorp, Homestead Park, and Pageview, among others. eNCA, in a noon SAST Monday report attributing the update to City Power, said electricity had been restored to the SABC, Netcare Garden City Hospital, and approximately half of Crown's industrial area, that residents and businesses in Mayfair West, Amalgam, Vrededorp, and Pageview remained without electricity because of ongoing cable faults, and that power to Sentech remained switched off for further maintenance and safety checks. No official restoration time for the remaining areas or for Sentech was given. Earlier Monday, City Power's Hursthill SDC bulletin issued at 7:30 a.m. SAST did not list the Mayfair Substation 16-hour emergency shutdown among current outages. In a Sunday, Nov 15, Mayfair Substation customer alert posted at 12:15 p.m. SAST, City Power said it would implement a 16-hour emergency shutdown from 12:00 noon Sunday to complete critical repairs at the Mayfair Substation; the planned window would have run until 4:00 a.m. SAST Monday. The same Monday 7:30 a.m. Hursthill bulletin said the centre was managing 1,524 open calls, 1,266 of them more than 24 hours old (a wider Hursthill service-area figure, not a customer count for the Mayfair outage alone). It also reported other Hursthill-area outages, including an investigation in Coronationville, Westbury, Newclare, and Paarlshoop (reported Sunday, no customer count); the Roosevelt Substation (Emmarentia Distributor) outage, about 75% restored, with customers particularly along Barry, Hertzog, and Muirfield remaining off until repairs were complete; and Industria Substation outages. In a 7:35 a.m. SAST Monday Roodepoort SDC bulletin, City Power said one load centre at Florida Substation would remain off until repairs were completed for customers in Florida Lake, Hamberg, and Georginia, and that loadshedding remains suspended until further notice.
outages.etr: No official restoration time was given for remaining Mayfair-area customers, parts of Crown, or Sentech. For the Roosevelt Substation outage in parts of Emmarentia, City Power said Monday morning that repairs were scheduled that morning and that customers particularly along Barry, Hertzog, and Muirfield would remain off until repairs were complete. For the Florida Lake, Hamberg, and Georginia outage, City Power said Monday morning that one load centre would remain off until repairs were completed and gave no restoration time.
outages.updated: Nov 16, 2026, SABC News 10:01 a.m. SAST Monday (= 2:01 a.m. CT), quoting City Power spokesperson Isaac Mangena; eNCA noon SAST Monday (= 4:00 a.m. CT); Hursthill SDC bulletin 7:30 a.m. SAST Monday (= 11:30 p.m. CT Sunday) and Roodepoort SDC bulletin 7:35 a.m. SAST Monday (= 11:35 p.m. CT Sunday); rechecked 5:55 AM CT Monday, no official customer count and no later official restoration time for remaining areas or Sentech

outages.cause: Drone attacks on power stations and other electricity infrastructure during the war between the Rapid Support Forces and the Sudanese Armed Forces
outages.affected: No official customer count. Al Jazeera, in a Nov 15 report, said the RSF has intensified attacks on power stations around Khartoum state over the past month, creating an energy crisis in the capital, and that there is no clear schedule for the resulting power cuts, which can last anywhere between six hours and a day. It said that between Oct 20 and Nov 2, 2026, there were at least 18 attacks on electricity infrastructure across at least nine states, leading to declining power generation capacity and fuel shortages. Citing The Associated Press, it said repeated drone attacks on power stations have seen electricity generation fall from about 4,400 megawatts before the war to about 1,100 MW today. Residents and a small-business owner in Port Sudan described prolonged, unreliable cuts, including outages lasting more than 24 hours. The UN resident and humanitarian coordinator, Denise Brown, was quoted warning that repeated strikes on power and fuel stations were disrupting dialysis, hospital births, and operations. No later official national customer count or restoration timetable was found.
outages.updated: Nov 15, 2026 (Al Jazeera feature, published Nov 15); generation figure attributed to The Associated Press; rechecked 5:55 AM CT Monday, no later official national customer count or restoration timetable found
